newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Elf -led oil group sees fast Caspian start.
newsitem.headline: Elf -led oil group sees fast Caspian start.

text.p: An international oil consortium led by France's Elf Aquitaine will start test drilling by the end of this year on two oil fields in the Azeri sector of the Caspian Sea, an Elf official said on Thursday.

Elf Petroleum Azerbaijan General Manager Jean-Francois Daganaud said the $2 billion consortium, which is developing the Lenkoran-Deniz and Talysh-Deniz sites, would begin the drilling after seismic studies were completed.
Elf and Total signed a production-sharing contract with Azeri state oil company SOCAR for the fields earlier this year.
Elf has a 40 percent stake in the project, Germany's Veba unit Deminex 10 percent, Iran's OIEC 10 percent, Total 10 percent and Petrofina of Belgium five percent. SOCAR has 25 percent.
The 30-year project, which has been approved by Azerbaijan's parliament, involves an area of 420 square km in waters up to 100 meters deep in the south end of the Azeri sea sector.
Daganaud said approximate reserves were estimated at about 50 million tonnes of crude but cautioned this was only a preliminary figure.
Output may reach 25 million tonnes a year (500,000 barrels per day).
